scope: For every one of the 23 knowledge-relevant generators cataloged in audit/generator-dependencies-v2.json (Phase 2A): which canonical domains it consumes, which migration wave that places it in (the MAX wave among its consumed domains, per audit/migration-waves.json — a generator cannot safely rely on the canonical model until every domain it reads has migrated), and a categorical (low/medium/high) migration complexity with a stated justification.
complexityMethod: LOW: few domains (1-2), no dataset redundancy or enriched/unenriched inconsistency found for this generator's reads. MEDIUM: 3+ domains, OR consumes a domain with a confirmed parallel/duplicate dataset requiring reconciliation, but its current rendered behavior is already correct. HIGH: consumes a domain where migration would CHANGE the generator's rendered output because it currently reads an inconsistent/incorrect data source (the enriched-vs-unenriched split) or has the highest domain fan-out in the graph. Every classification below cites which of these criteria applied.

generators.justification: Highest domain fan-out of any generator in the graph (11 of 18 domains) — the master generator identified in Phase 1A as the site's single largest blast-radius file (3,679 lines). High complexity reflects breadth of impact, not a data-inconsistency bug — this generator already reads the enriched/correct sources today.

Confirmed in Phase 2A to read data/names.json (unenriched) while the logically-identical embedded copy inside generate-programmatic-pages.js reads data/names-enriched.json. Migrating this generator to the canonical model will CHANGE its rendered output (origin pool currently under-populated relative to its sibling implementation) — a behavior change, not a pure data-source swap.

The flagship instance of the origin-dual-file-split (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json): reads unenriched data/names.json, producing a 100% origin-fallback rate on its own pages versus 95.6% on name-detail-page for the identical concept (Phase 1C/1D). Migration will materially change rendered content for all 150 live sibling-harmony pages — the highest-behavior-change-risk generator in this matrix.

Low domain count within Name Entity scope, but its primary subject (surname) has no canonical schema yet (Phase 2A explicitly deferred a Surname Entity). Classified medium rather than low because its migration is blocked on out-of-scope future work, not because the Name-Entity-side dependency is complex.

Confirmed to NOT read data/country-differentials.json at all (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json compare-page-orphaned-dataset) — its migration is simpler than its apparent field overlap suggests, since there is no second data source to reconcile, only relationships.comparisonPairs to populate from its existing independent computation.

Narrow, single-purpose need (relatedNames.equivalents[] only). Must wait for relatedNames' wave (3) under whole-domain migration ordering even though its own specific sub-field has no dependency on origin/classification/popularity — noted as a documented ordering conservatism, not a complexity driver.
Simple aggregation over one researched domain; no redundancy or inconsistency found for this generator specifically.
Same profile as generate-popularity-pages.js.

The one page-generator confirmed to read BOTH data/regional-trend-acceleration.json and data/country-differentials.json — two of the three parallel popularity-derived datasets (audit/knowledge-redundancy.json popularity-three-parallel-derivations). Its migration requires reconciling two independently-computed sources into one popularity.trendAcceleration value, unlike the single-source popularity-pages generators above.
Data-build script, single source domain, no page-rendering risk.

Same profile as generate-country-differentials.js — both derive independently from popularity.records, which is itself a noted redundancy (see audit/dataset-transition-map.json), but neither script's OWN migration is complex in isolation.

Already performs exactly the single-merge pattern the canonical model requires (audit/knowledge-domains.json: 'this merge happens once, upstream of ALL generators, by construction'). Its migration is closer to a no-op than a rewrite.
Already the correct write-path for the canonical origin/language domains per docs/CANONICAL_KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.md's ownership rules; no current dataset redundancy involves this script directly.
Single deterministic rule-based output domain, no redundancy found.
Sole real entry point for popularity research; no parallel producer to reconcile.

One of two current parallel producers of variants.spellingVariants[] (alongside scripts/acquire/build-variants.js) and pronunciation.syllableCount (alongside data/names.json's own syllables field) — exhaustively confirmed identical output in Phase 2A, but the migration must still formally reconcile two producers into one, which is inherently more complex than a single-producer field even when their current output agrees.

domainsConsumed: (none — writes a scoring ruleset, not domain data)
generators.justification: Produces configuration consumed by relationships.surnameCompatibility[].score, not entity data itself — not wave-gated, analogous to metadata.dataCompletenessScore's exception in audit/migration-waves.json.
Parallel producer to normalize-names.js for the identical canonical field — same reconciliation note applies.

Its own header comment documents an enriched-then-base fallback pattern, but only for identity-level fields (name/slug), which carry no risk of the kind found in generate-sibling-pages.js — the fallback here cannot produce a wrong fact, only a slightly different name-selection order for the explorer grid.
Consumes only identity.slug for URL enumeration; earliest possible migration wave of any generator in this matrix.

The actual scoring engine invoked by generate-sibling-pages.js. Its documented weights (origin 30%, rhythm 25%, popularity 20%, style 10%) mean its real inputs will change value (not just source file) once fed a canonical record with populated origin.cluster — the score itself would shift for any pair where origin currently defaults to the 'various origins' fallback.
Purely phonetic scoring of the name string; its surname-side input is out of Name Entity scope but introduces no complexity on this schema's side.

Placed at the graph's terminal wave because it writes citations (which depend on meaning already existing). Phase 2A found its output columns (meaning_source, origin_source, confidence_score) are present-but-always-null in live data/normalized-names.json, suggesting this script may not be currently wired into the live build path — its migration complexity includes verifying/reconnecting it, not only remapping its fields.
